notes: Archives is the glass map. Sixteen breakable panes plus ten doors means cover is provisional here in a way it is nowhere else -- a wall that protected you a moment ago stops existing once somebody shoots it.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: Much of the apparent cover is breakable glass, so a position that worked once will not survive being contested; cover has to be re-judged after every exchange.
nuance.because: The arena carries sixteen Glass records, the most of any multiplayer stage.

nuance.claim: Clearing glass on purpose opens firing lines that did not exist and denies an opponent a position they were relying on, which is a stronger opening move here than seeking a fight.
nuance.because: The arena's sixteen Glass records are destructible props rather than fixed geometry.

nuance.claim: Breaking glass announces both your position and that a sightline has changed, so it is never a free action.
Eight spawn points is too many to hold, so effort goes into controlling the stairs and doorways rather than reappearance points.
nuance.because: The arena carries eight Spawn records, joint most of any stage.

nuance.claim: The stage runs over more than one floor connected by stairs, so opponents arrive from above and below as often as along a corridor.
Desks and fittings split the floors into lanes, giving genuine cover that, unlike the glass, does not disappear when shot.
nuance.because: The arena carries eleven StandardProp records alongside its glass.

nuance.claim: Pickups are the normalised conversion set, so neither armour nor ammunition is worth fighting over and the map is decided on position.
nuance.because: The arena carries the standard conversion loadout of two Armour, sixteen AmmoBox and nine Collectable records.

nuance.claim: Ten doors across a two-floor stage means movement between areas is predictable enough to watch or mine.
nuance.because: The arena carries ten Door records.

nuance.claim: A mine placed where glass has already been broken catches players taking the new route, which they treat as safe precisely because it is new.
There are long sightlines here, but firing along one reveals the position and the glass around it will be broken shortly after, so a sniping spot is good for one or two shots rather than a match.
With one-hit kills, standing behind glass is standing in the open, because a single round through it is lethal and it does not stop rounds anyway.
A carrier breaks pursuit by changing floors, since the stairs are the one place the map's long sightlines do not reach.
